claims.claim_en: The verb in the ayah (فَنَادَتْهُ) derives from the root ن و د. The base lemma نَادَى corresponds to the pattern fāʿala (often treated as Form III), i.e. a causative/reciprocal 'call' pattern; in the ayah it appears as a past verb with a clitic pronoun.

claims.claim_ar: الاسم «يَحْيَى» من الجذر ح ي ي، معناه المرتبط بالحيَاة — الأصل الدلالي: «يَحْيَى» = ‹يَحيا/الحيّ› أي ذو حياة أو سيعيش.
claims.claim_en: The proper name Yaḥyā (يَحْيَى) comes from the root ḥ-y-y meaning 'to live'. The name denotes 'the living' / 'he will live'.

claims.needs_review_reason: The exact morphological nuance (pattern vocalization and emphatic doubling) can vary in transmission; the source confirms the prophetic sense but not full morphological parsing of the nisba/formation.
